To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
age moderates the effects of CCT on measures of cognitive, symptom, & functional change over time in individuals with severe mental illnesses.

1) age moderated the effects of compensatory cognitive training on cognitive, symptom and functional outcomes; and 2) the effects of CCT on cognition and functioning were stronger for younger participants, whereas CCT had greater effects on symptom severity for older participants.

Age was a moderator of change following a 12-week cognitive compensatory training program for individuals with severe mental illnesses; younger participants showed improvement on cognitive measures of verbal fluency and financial capacity, and older participants showed reduced symptom severity and less functional decline.
